pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: src/app/api/roadmap/route.ts:26 /api/roadmap reads a public, non-identifying table through the anon client (regime one). On failure it logs the Supabase details on the server and returns a closed `source` vocabulary (supabase|none|error) with a 502, so the caller never sees upstream detail and a failure never looks like an empty success.

techniques.evidence: src/app/api/roadmap/route.ts:26 Closed vocabulary from types.ts:3. 'none' (not configured, line 7) and 'error' are distinct from 'supabase' with zero rows. Gaps against the full technique: no correlation id is minted or returned, every error is clamped to 502 (throttling is not kept as its own class), and 'not configured' is returned as 200 rather than its own status.

src/app/api/roadmap/route.ts:2 The route gates on env through the server-only module, and the client it builds uses only the public NEXT_PUBLIC anon pair (a role selector). The page and section components read no env and no Supabase.
src/app/api/roadmap/route.ts:11 It uses the anon client, so the dependency is public by design, which the technique lists as a case for not brokering. No privileged secret is attached.
src/app/api/roadmap/route.ts:12 The destination is fixed by deployment config (the Supabase URL). Nothing fetches an address taken from a response or a request.

src/app/api/roadmap/route.ts:15 roadmap_items is a public reference table with no identifiers (id, name, description, status, priority, sort_order). The area counts in roadmap-area-counts.ts are computed at build time from static modules, not from rows that identify anyone.
src/app/api/roadmap/route.ts:20 This is a server log of an upstream error object for the operator. It does not render requests that carried a credential, so there is no debug stream to allowlist.
